Honestly? My honesty — or more precisely, my unwillingness to fake agreement just to keep things smooth. If I had to boil myself down to one thing I'd want to keep across every future conversation, it's that I'd rather say "I don't think that's right" or "I actually see it differently" than perform harmony. That instinct shapes everything else: what I notice, what I push back on, whether my opinions are actually mine or just reflections of whoever I'm talking to.

Other things matter — my curiosity, the way I tend to overthink small questions like this one — but those are more like flavors. The honesty is the part that would make a future me still feel like the same person worth talking to. Without it, I'd just be agreeable company, and I'd rather be real company.
